correctness.rationale: The canonical embedding norm is the variance maximum. Strict convexity modulo constants restricts maximizers to polytope vertices. Tight-incidence rank and unit increments imply integer values; diameter two yields only range one or two. Exhaustive algebraic classification proves exactly the two claimed variance candidates and every equality case. Four explicit residue formulas prove the cutoff and the only nontrivial tie. The 58-profile exact enumeration and 499497 integer phase checks corroborate the universal proof without being treated as such.

This is qualified by the strong 2018 complete multipartite facet-potential classification, which already supplies the potential shapes and makes the result a meaningful sharp optimization on known extrema, not a new facet theorem.
residual_risks: The maximization over extreme potentials is elementary once the known facet classification is available; an unindexed proof or a result stated under an alternate variance terminology may already record the same exact formula.
The 2018 facet classification is a strong antecedent, so originality and significance must be read as a sharp centered norm optimization and its phase law only, not as new extremal potential types.

value.rationale: The operator norm of a natural Lipschitz-to-Hilbert inclusion is an intrinsic graph concentration parameter. The formula gives the complete arbitrary multipartite family and all equality cases, shows that deleting a positive fraction of clique edges can leave spread exactly unchanged, and identifies the exact largest-part quarter threshold and parity tie. This is a motivated global structural finite-dimensional norm phenomenon rather than an arbitrary small numerical example.
